orphan_risk.details: If production 'Charge' / 'charges' table exists with rows whose caseId does not match criminal_cases.caseId, the charges_caseId_fkey FK creation will fail. Must verify data integrity before migration.
orphan_risk.verification_command: SELECT c."caseId" FROM "Charge" c LEFT JOIN criminal_cases cc ON c."caseId" = cc."caseId" WHERE cc."caseId" IS NULL;

destructive_operations.assessment: No destructive operations. Migration is additive + rename.

charge_table_existence.details: No previous migration creates a 'Charge' table. The Charge model existed in schema.prisma (without @@map) since the persistence layer migration, but was never included in any CREATE TABLE migration. The migration SQL references ALTER TABLE "Charge" which will fail if the table does not exist.

scenarios.scenario: Table 'Charge' does NOT exist in production DB
scenarios.result: ALTER TABLE "Charge" fails with ERROR: relation "Charge" does not exist
scenarios.fix: Replace ALTER+RENAME with CREATE TABLE "charges" directly

scenarios.scenario: Table 'Charge' exists (created manually or via prisma db push)
scenarios.result: ALTER and RENAME succeed, then FK constraints applied
scenarios.risk: FK on caseId may fail if orphan rows exist

scenarios.result: ALTER TABLE "Charge" fails because PostgreSQL quoted identifiers are case-sensitive. "Charge" != "charge"
scenarios.fix: Use ALTER TABLE "charge" instead, or verify exact table name in production

charge_table_existence.recommended_pre_check: SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename IN ('Charge', 'charge', 'charges');

existing_api_impact.details: All existing APIs use prisma.charge.* which Prisma maps to the @@map table name. After migration, Prisma will query 'charges' table. If migration succeeds, all existing APIs work without code changes.
